code: char *str = malloc(size+1); memcpy(str, data, size); str[size] = 0;
note: Attacker-controlled SSML input bytes are copied into a heap buffer and NUL-terminated, then passed to espeak_Synth with espeakSSML flag.
The '<' character starts SSML tag parsing; the following character must be '/', alphabetic, '!', or '?' to enter tag processing.

code: while (!Eof() && (c1 != '>') && (n_xml_buf < N_XML_BUF)) { xml_buf[n_xml_buf++] = c1; c1 = GetC(); }
note: Tag content is read into the stack array wchar_t xml_buf[N_XML_BUF+1] (501 elements) until '>' or 500 chars; a NUL is written at xml_buf[n_xml_buf].
The 500-character tag buffer (with NUL at index 500) is passed to ProcessSsmlTag for tag/attribute parsing.

code: for (ix = 0; ix < (sizeof(tag_name)-1); ix++) { if (((c = xml_buf[ix]) == 0) || iswspace(c)) break; tag_name[ix] = tolower((char)c); }
note: Tag name 'speak' is extracted (5 chars), so ix=5 and px=&xml_buf[5] points to the attribute region.
px points to the attributes area; for a 500-char tag ending in 'xml:lang', px points to 487 spaces followed by 'xml:lang' then NUL at index 500.
First attribute lookup for 'xml:base' scans the whole buffer, finds no match, and returns NULL; no OOB occurs here.
GetVoiceAttributes is invoked for the <speak> tag and calls GetSsmlAttribute with name="xml:lang" on the same px pointer.
The scan advances pw through the spaces; when pw reaches the 'x' of 'xml:lang' at index 492, pw[-1] is a space, so the attribute-name comparison begins.
The 8 characters 'xml:lang' match name[0..7]; at ix=8, name[8] is '\0' and *pw reads xml_buf[500] which is also '\0', so the loop continues.

After matching the NUL at index 500, pw is incremented to &xml_buf[501] and ix becomes 9; the next *pw dereference reads one wchar_t past the end of the 501-element stack array xml_buf, causing a stack-buffer-overflow READ.
